doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

title: Father's jam sessions, Clifford Brown and Bobby Mojica
summary: Asked for an AHA moment, Brecker describes his pianist father's jam sessions, record collection, neighbors, Bobby Mojica and Clifford Brown in Philly, and his wariness of music as a life.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Um hum. The idea of hearing — you were born in ’45 — maybe 1955 there is so much going on in the jazz world, was there an AHA moment for you that — a person or an LP that really propelled you into the career?

Well that’s a good question. Like I said, my father was a semi-professional pianist, very good songwriter/singer, knew a lot of musicians in Philly and there were jam sessions at the house. And the level was really pretty damn high. He had a great record collection. By luck our next door neighbor was a fine tenor player and his sister was a good jazz singer, and people would come over generally. There was a very good trumpet player named Bobby Mojica who had a good career in Detroit as a trumpet player, also was a businessman but he was a great trumpet player. Clifford Brown was alive and well in Philly during those years actually, and he was the talk of the town always. They had a kind of home base in Philadelphia and played there quite a bit. So I just grew up with it. And I don’t know if there was an AHA moment because I always — if anything I tried to
get interested in other things because it seemed like the music life so to speak was rather up and down.
